question.worked_solution:
Using the linearity property of double integrals, we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}(1-3{x}^{2}+2y)\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{R}\text{d}A-{∬}_{R}3{x}^{2}\text{ }\text{d}A+{∬}_{R}2y\text{ }\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

The first integral is the double integral of unity:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}\text{d}A=\text{Area}(R)=2\cdot 1=2\end{aligned}
$$

 

The function under the second integral is independent of $y.$ So, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}3{x}^{2}\text{ }\text{d}A & =(1-0){\int }_{-1}^{1}3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =[{x}^{3}]_{-1}^{1} \\  & ={1}^{3}-(-1)^{3} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

The function under the third integral is independent of $x.$ So, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}2y\text{ }\text{d}A & =(1-(-1)){\int }_{0}^{1}2y\,\text{d}y \\  & =2[{y}^{2}]_{0}^{1} \\  & =2({1}^{2}-{0}^{2}) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, combining our results, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}(1-3{x}^{2}+2y)\,\text{d}A=2-2+2=2.\end{aligned}
$$
